primaryChecks.text: The sons of Reuben, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, of valiant men, men able to bear buckler and sword, able to shoot with bow, and skillful in war, were forty-four thousand seven hundred sixty that were able to go out to war.
primaryChecks.previousContext: All these were listed by genealogies in the days of Jotham king of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam king of Israel.
primaryChecks.nextContext: They made war with the Hagrites, with Jetur, and Naphish, and Nodab.
primaryChecks.decisionJa: 文脈上の地理句との関係はあり得るが固有名の明記がなく、無理に同定しない。

primaryChecks.text: The children of the half-tribe of Manasseh lived in the land. They increased from Bashan to Baal Hermon, Senir, and Mount Hermon.
primaryChecks.previousContext: For many fell slain, because the war was of God. They lived in their place until the captivity.
primaryChecks.nextContext: These were the heads of their fathers’ houses: Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, and Jahdiel—mighty men of valor, famous men, heads of their fathers’ houses.
primaryChecks.decisionJa: 文脈上の地理句との関係はあり得るが固有名の明記がなく、無理に同定しない。

primaryChecks.text: So the God of Israel stirred up the spirit of Pul king of Assyria, and the spirit of Tilgath Pilneser king of Assyria, and he carried away the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, and brought them to Halah, Habor, Hara, and to the river of Gozan, to this day.
primaryChecks.previousContext: They trespassed against the God of their fathers, and played the prostitute after the gods of the peoples of the land whom God destroyed before them.
primaryChecks.decisionJa: 文脈上の地理句との関係はあり得るが固有名の明記がなく、無理に同定しない。
